scope: Append-only reconciliation of two P2 source changes against a frozen P3 source snapshot; not a current P3 green gate, provider, evaluation, chemistry, replication, training, paper, release, or SOTA result.

historical_validator.command: env -u PYTHONPATH conda run --no-capture-output -n chemsmart python scripts/review/validate_frontier_program.py --repo .

supported: The unchanged historical P3 validator reports exactly two later source-hash drifts.
Those two current source hashes exactly match the P2 firewall addendum.
qualified: The frozen P3 record remains a valid historical fixture-only source snapshot.
unresolved: A reviewed current-source P3 validation, provider capability, evaluation, chemistry, replication, and all P5/P6 evidence surfaces.
rejected: Treating the historical P3 validator as green for the current patched source or promoting any program gate from this provenance delta.

failure_ledger.failure: The frozen P3 validator reported source-hash drift after the later P2 firewall repair.
failure_ledger.hypothesis: P3 correctly pins its historical source snapshot and cannot know whether a later change is reviewed without losing its own hash boundary.
failure_ledger.minimal_change: Preserve P3 byte-for-byte and add a separate validator that permits only the two P2-pinned drifts.
failure_ledger.evidence: One unchanged historical-validator invocation, the frozen P3 receipt, and the P2 firewall receipt/source hashes.
failure_ledger.result: Historical-red and current P2 integrity are reported separately; no original P3 data was changed.
failure_ledger.limitation: This does not create a current P3 green validation or repair any P3/P5/P6 blocker.
failure_ledger.rollback_boundary: Delete only this delta; any later source change requires a new delta and must not alter the historical P3 receipt or validator.

phase_close_validation.command: env -u PYTHONPATH conda run --no-capture-output -n chemsmart python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/agent/runtime/test_frontier_p2_p3_historical_source_compatibility.py -q
